tagline: For small WooCommerce shops on PayPal: refunds, disputes and unpaid invoices in one conversation, and no money moves without the owner’s yes.
introNote: PayPal runs on the real PayPal sandbox in this video (PayPal's public default sandbox app). The Money Desk analytics use labelled mock data.

steps.text: If you run a small WooCommerce shop on PayPal, refunds, disputes and unpaid invoices sit in separate screens, and one wrong refund costs real money. Tillwise is a store agent you simply talk to. It shows you the numbers, and it moves money only after you confirm. Here, refunds go to the real PayPal sandbox.
Money never moves on a guess. The refund is previewed first, and when the owner says go ahead, the host asks once more before the PayPal call is made.
Under the hood, every MCP tool call is visible: the preview, the confirmation, then the refund call to the PayPal sandbox, and its audit row with PayPal's refund ID.

This is the Money Desk, built inside AG Studio. The grid at the top is live: every PayPal sandbox object Tillwise created, with the refund we just made at the top. Below it, built-in charts sit next to three custom widgets: refund rate, who still owes us, and dispute deadlines. Those analytics run on a labelled mock ledger.

Studio's AI panel runs on the GitHub Copilot SDK. The model reads a read-only refund anomaly tool on that mock ledger, quotes its figures, and adds a chart of refunds per day by reason, so the damaged mug shipments stand out against the week before.
The Studio agent is read-only: it has no tool that moves money. Refunds happen only in the voice flow, after a preview and the owner’s yes.
Tillwise and PayPal. Talk to your shop, see your money, and stay in control of every refund.
